evidence.reason: scanPatch derives the path from `+++`/`---` headers by only stripping an unquoted `a/` or `b/` prefix. Git C-quotes non-ASCII paths by default, so a path such as `secrét.env` remains `"b/..."` with quotes and backslash escapes. A path-specific rule like `\.env$` then fails to match, even though removed deletion lines are scanned by this function; the later entry scan excludes deletions, so absent gitleaks the removed secret can escape installation. Decoding Git-quoted paths before rule matching (and refusing unsafe/undecodable paths) is a routine correctness fix in existing intended behavior.
